SparkR / SPARKR-202
Default AMI Needs Updating, EC2 Scripts Fail
Issue Type: Bug
Assignee: Unassigned
Components: Deployment
Created: 17/Feb/15 12:53 PM
Environment:

Amazon EC2
Priority: Major
Reporter: Amos

The current Amazon EC2 script is dysfunctional, and the AMI is seriously outdated. A few issues:

  • The EC2 security profile needs to open port 7077 on the master.
  • R on the AMI is at version 3.1.1, and was installed without a BLAS lib. Besides the speed issue (people should at least have the option of switching to an optimized BLAS), some packages, such as `slam`, simply won't compile unless R is built with a shared BLAS library.

Then there's this: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/27039954/intermittent-timeout-exception-using-spark, and some other similar questions on stackoverflow, where the solution seems to require disabling the firewall completely.

(I still can't get this problem to go away, even after disabling the firewall!)

But either way, with the version of R on the ami, its in serious need of an update.

Re: Default AMI Needs Updating, EC2 Scripts Fail

Amos Thanks for reporting this. Couple of points

  • The spark_ec2.py script is not maintained in SparkR and we just use the ones provided by the Spark project. It'll be great if you can open an issue on https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK for the firewall not being setup properly
  • For the R install we just use the one provided by the OS by running `yum install -y R` . Its unfortunate that this doesn't have a BLAS lib installed with it. I am not very familiar with rebuilding R with BLAS support. Do you have any pointers on how it should be done ?

There are a couple of configure flags that you'd probably want to set. It's very easy. An AMI should probably also have many of the common packages preinstalled. It would not hurt to put rstudio server on the master either.

If you want, I have an image that you could adapt by adding the stuff so it works with the spark scripts. Or if you have an image, and want to set up a small instance, I'm happy to go in and set the thing up myself for you. I'd really like to be contributing to the project in whatever way I can.

I also suggest that perhaps the instruction page might be amended to explain how the security settings have to change for the images to work.

Sure feel free to send me an email. FWIW the steps I used to launch the cluster were

1. Clone the Spark repo from github.com/apache/spark
2. cd spark/ec2
3. ./spark-ec2 -s 2 -t r3.xlarge -i <key_file> -k <key_name> -r us-west-2 -z us-west-2c launch my-security-group

I used us-west-2 but I don't think that should matter.
